docs.title: ✨ What is FixMyMedTech?
docs.text:
A platform that gives biomedical engineers the knowledge, tools, and community to diagnose, repair, and maintain medical equipment — anywhere on the continent.

Fix My MedTech is an open-source platform where biomedical engineers tag, track, diagnose, and repair medical devices. It is built around the realities of the field: devices that arrive without manuals, without spare parts, and often already degraded — in environments where heat, humidity, dust and unstable power accelerate failure far beyond what manufacturers expect.

docs.title: Our Pledge
docs.text:
We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

docs.title: Our Standards
docs.text:
Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:

  • Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
  • Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
  • Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
  • Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
  • Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community

Examples of unacceptable behavior include:

  • The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
  • Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
  • Public or private harassment
  • Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
  • Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting

docs.title: Enforcement Responsibilities
docs.text:
Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces. Examples of representing our community include using an official e-mail address, posting via an official social media account, or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the community leaders responsible for enforcement at hello@careagain.org. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

docs.title: Enforcement Guidelines
docs.text: Community leaders will follow these Community Impact Guidelines in determining the consequences for any action they deem in violation of this Code of Conduct:

docs.title: 1. Correction
docs.text:
Community Impact: Use of inappropriate language or other behavior deemed unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

Consequence: A private, written warning from community leaders, providing clarity around the nature of the violation and an explanation of why the behavior was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.

docs.title: 2. Warning
docs.text:
Community Impact: A violation through a single incident or series of actions.

Consequence: A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, for a specified period of time. This includes avoiding interactions in community spaces as well as external channels like social media. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.

docs.title: 3. Temporary Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: A serious violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior.

Consequence: A temporary ban from any sort of interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. No public or private interaction with the people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct, is allowed during this period. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.

docs.title: 4. Permanent Ban
docs.text:
Community Impact: Demonstrating a pattern of violation of community standards, including sustained inappropriate behavior, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.

Consequence: A permanent ban from any sort of public interaction within the community.

docs.title: FixMyMedTech — Architecture Guide
docs.text:
Medical equipment management platform for LMICs (Low and Middle Income Countries).

Stack: FastAPI (REST API, auth, admin portal, reverse proxy) + FastHTML (server-rendered UI) + PostgreSQL + MinIO (object storage).

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text:
Browser (HTTPS)
   │
   ▼
nginx ──► Backend FastAPI  :8888          ← single public entry point
              ├─ /api/*     REST API + auth
              ├─ /admin     SQLAdmin portal (superusers only)
              ├─ /docs      Swagger
              ├─ /health
              └─ /{path}    reverse proxy → FastHTML frontend (frontend:5001)
                                │  server-side httpx, Bearer token
                                ▼
                         Backend /api/*
                                │
              ┌─────────────────┴─────────────────┐
              ▼                                   ▼
   PostgreSQL (local or Supabase)        MinIO (device / fault / avatar photos)

FastHTML is not a traditional frontend — it is a Python web server that renders HTML server-side. There is no JavaScript framework and no build step. The browser never calls the API directly: it talks to FastHTML (through the backend proxy), and FastHTML calls the API server-side.

docs.title: The backend as proxy hub
docs.text: Every request reaches the FastAPI backend first. The catch-all route in backend/main.py forwards anything that is not admin, docs, redoc, openapi.json, health or api/* to http://frontend:5001, adding X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Proto so the frontend can build correct absolute URLs (e.g. device QR links). The backend runs with --forwarded-allow-ips "*" so URLs behind nginx are generated as https://….

docs.title: Frontend feature pattern
docs.text:
Each feature in frontend/features/<feature>/ contains:

  • api.py — thin async wrappers over backend endpoints, built on the helpers in config/api.py. Errors are raised as httpx.HTTPStatusError carrying the backend's detail message.
  • pages/*.py (or pages.py) — each module defines rt = APIRouter() and its route handlers, rendering with the shells from components.py (page_shell for logged-in pages, pub_shell for public QR pages, auth_shell for login/signup).

Every page router is registered in frontend/main.py with module.rt.to_app(app). Registration order matters when patterns overlap (e.g. /profile/photo must be registered before /profile/{profile_id}).

All user-visible text goes through i18n.py: _ = t(lang) then _("key"), with lang taken from the session (switchable via POST /lang).

docs.title: Why two servers?
docs.text:
FastHTML handles routing and rendering; FastAPI handles data and business logic.

  • The API can be used independently by mobile apps or third parties later.
  • Authorization and business rules live in one place (the API).
  • FastHTML stays thin — it fetches data and renders HTML.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• Accounts are local, managed by FastAPI-Users (backend/config/users.py) with JWT bearer tokens signed with AUTH_JWT_SECRET. Optional Google / GitHub / Discord OAuth is configured in backend/config/oauth.py.
  • On login, FastHTML stores the JWT in its session cookie (req.session["token"], signed with SESSION_SECRET) and sends it as an Authorization: Bearer header on every server-side API call. The browser never sends API requests itself.
  • Protected endpoints use Depends(get_current_profile) (backend/utils/profile.py), which loads the caller's Profile together with their organization memberships. Public endpoints use get_optional_profile or no dependency at all.
  • The /admin SQLAdmin portal has its own session login restricted to users with is_superuser = true.

docs.title: Organizations and roles
docs.text:
Users belong to one or more organizations through org_users, and the role is per organization:

Role What they can do superuser (account flag) Everything, including the /admin portal admin Manage the organization, its members, devices; assign and approve faults technician Register devices, diagnose/repair faults, log maintenance engineering_staff Like technician; can be assigned faults clinical_staff Scan QR codes, view device info, report faults

A device is linked to two organizations:

  • organization_maintenance_id — the organization that maintains it (receives its fault reports);
  • healthsite_id — the hospital/clinic where it is installed (approves repair quotes).

docs.title: Fault workflow
docs.text:
Fault reports move through steps, each performed by a different person (see the header of backend/routers/fault_reports.py):

open ──(maintenance-org admin assigns)──► assigned
     ──(assignee: diagnosis + quote)────► diagnosed
     ──(healthsite admin approves)──────► approved      (rejection → back to assigned)
     ──(assignee repairs, final price)──► resolved

in_progress is an optional step when the assignee goes on site. A device without a healthsite is approved by the maintenance-org admin.

docs.title: Document library
docs.text:
Manuals and guides live in fixmymedtech.documents, and devices link to them through device_documents (many to many), so one manual serves every device of that model. A document is either:

  • from iFixit (source = 'ifixit'): a link to a PDF in the iFixit library, found by manufacturer and model. The file is never copied; the row stores the URL and iFixit ids, once per iFixit document. Metadata always comes from iFixit itself (backend/config/ifixit.py, cached for a day).
  • uploaded (source = 'upload'): a PDF stored in MinIO. Uploads start with contribution_status = 'pending'; sending them to the iFixit library after a superuser's approval is planned.

Anyone can read documents (device page, public QR page, /library). Attaching, uploading and removing need a logged-in user. Uploads are limited to PDFs of DOCUMENT_MAX_MB (50 MB by default); the nginx client_max_body_size in front of the app must allow that size.

docs.title: Feedback button
docs.text: Every page shows a ? button (bottom-right) with two choices, Send feedback and Report an issue. Both open the /feedback form, which works with or without login. POST /api/feedback/ stores the report in fixmymedtech.feedback first, then posts it in the background to a Discord forum channel through a webhook, creating one thread per report (backend/config/discord.py). The outcome is recorded in discord_status (sent, failed, or disabled when no webhook is configured), and every report is visible in the admin portal under Feedback. Email addresses are never posted to Discord.

docs.title: Device photos
docs.text: Uploads are EXIF-corrected, downscaled and re-encoded as JPEG (Pillow), then stored in MinIO. A background task produces a white-background variant (local rembg, or Gemini if GEMINI_API_KEY is set). Disable it with AUTO_PROCESS_PHOTO=off.

docs.title: Data flow — QR scan (no login)
docs.text:
1. Nurse scans the QR on a device
2. Browser opens https://{domain}/d/{device_id}  (backend proxies to FastHTML)
3. FastHTML calls GET {API_URL}/api/devices/public/{device_id}
4. FastAPI reads PostgreSQL (no auth required for this endpoint)
5. FastHTML renders device info, documentation and the fault report form
6. Nurse submits → FastHTML calls POST /api/faults/public
7. FastAPI stores the report; a high/critical severity sets the device status to "fault"

docs.title: Data flow — login
docs.text:
1. User submits the login form
2. FastHTML calls POST {API_URL}/api/auth/login
3. FastAPI-Users verifies the password and returns a JWT
4. FastHTML stores the JWT in its session cookie
5. Each later page fetches data server-side with Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
6. FastAPI validates it on every protected endpoint via Depends(get_current_profile)

docs.title: Attach a manual and search the library
docs.text:
Attach manuals to a device in two ways: link them from iFixit, or upload your own PDF. Anyone who scans the device's QR label can then open them. The Library searches every document in FixMyMedTech and on iFixit. The video is narrated and available in English, Spanish and French.

EnglishEspañolFrançais

  1. Go to Devices and tap Edit on the device.
  2. In the Documents card, choose how to add a manual:
    • Find on iFixit. The search starts from the device's manufacturer and model. Tick the manuals you want and tap Attach selected.
    • Upload a PDF. Add a title, a type and a language, choose the file (PDF, up to 50 MB) and tap Upload. Uploaded documents are public: never include patient information.
  3. The documents now show on the device page and on its public QR page.
  4. Open Library to search every manual by device, manufacturer or model. It lists documents already in FixMyMedTech (with how many devices use each one), then everything iFixit has. Filter by type to see only service manuals, user manuals or quick guides.

  1. Ve a Dispositivos y pulsa Editar en el equipo.
  2. En la tarjeta Documentos, elige cómo añadir un manual:
    • Buscar en iFixit. La búsqueda parte del fabricante y el modelo del equipo. Marca los manuales que quieras y pulsa Adjuntar seleccionados.
    • Subir un PDF. Pon un título, un tipo y un idioma, elige el archivo (PDF, hasta 50 MB) y pulsa Subir. Los documentos subidos son públicos: no incluyas nunca datos de pacientes.
  3. Los documentos aparecen en la página del equipo y en su página QR pública.
  4. Abre Biblioteca para buscar cualquier manual por equipo, fabricante o modelo. Muestra primero los documentos que ya están en FixMyMedTech (y cuántos equipos usan cada uno), y después todo lo que hay en iFixit. Filtra por tipo para ver solo manuales de servicio, de usuario o guías rápidas.

  1. Allez dans Appareils et touchez Modifier sur l'appareil.
  2. Dans la carte Documents, choisissez comment ajouter un manuel :
    • Chercher sur iFixit. La recherche part du fabricant et du modèle de l'appareil. Cochez les manuels voulus et touchez Joindre la sélection.
    • Téléverser un PDF. Indiquez un titre, un type et une langue, choisissez le fichier (PDF, 50 Mo maximum) et touchez Téléverser. Les documents téléversés sont publics : n'y mettez jamais d'informations sur les patients.
  3. Les documents apparaissent sur la page de l'appareil et sur sa page QR publique.
  4. Ouvrez Bibliothèque pour chercher un manuel par appareil, fabricant ou modèle. Elle affiche d'abord les documents déjà dans FixMyMedTech (et combien d'appareils utilisent chacun), puis tout ce que propose iFixit. Filtrez par type pour n'afficher que les manuels de service, d'utilisation ou les guides rapides.

Silent, shorter versions of each video are in docs/docs/videos/ (attach-manual-<lang>-mute.mp4).

docs.title: Collaborating on FixMyMedTech
docs.text:
FixMyMedTech is open source. Everyone is welcome to help: fixing bugs, adding features, improving translations, writing documentation, or testing on real hospital equipment.

The project lives at https://github.com/FixMyMedTech/fixmymedtech-app.

docs.title: 1. Reporting an issue
docs.text: All work is tracked with GitHub Issues. Open one at https://github.com/FixMyMedTech/fixmymedtech-app/issues/new.

docs.title: Before you open an issue
docs.text:
• Search the existing issues (open and closed) — your problem may already have an answer.
  • Use the applicable issue type (Bug report / Feature request / Question).

docs.title: Good bug reports include
docs.text:
• What you did — step-by-step reproduction.
  • What you expected vs. what happened.
  • Environment — browser/device, and which deployment (production platform.fixmymedtech.org or development dev.fixmymedtech.org).
  • Screenshots or a screen recording — a picture is worth 1000 words.
  • Any log output (browser console or docker compose logs backend).

docs.title: Good feature requests include
docs.text:
• The problem you are trying to solve, not just the solution you imagine.
  • Who it helps and why.
  • A rough proposal or mock-up if you have one.

Labels like bug, feature, documentation, good first issue help maintainers triage. If you are not sure where something belongs, just open the issue — we can always relabel it.

docs.title: 2. The collaboration flow
docs.text: Contributions go through the classic fork-and-PR flow. The screenshot below is the summary path we use:

docs.title: Where to branch from
docs.text:
• Development work targets the dev branch. Pushing to dev auto-deploys to the development server (dev.fixmymedtech.org).
  • main auto-deploys to production, so a maintainer merges approved PRs into main — do not push straight to it.
  • Start from an issue: “fixes #123” in the PR description links the work.

docs.title: Step by step
docs.text:
1. Find or create an issue and tell us you want to work on it.
  2. Fork FixMyMedTech/fixmymedtech-app (or add a remote to your own fork).
  3. Create a branch from dev, with a short descriptive name, e.g. fix/avatar-menu-stale-session.
  4. Make small, focused commits — one logical change per commit, with a clear message.
  5. Run the app locally and check your change before pushing (see Getting Started). The project has no automated test suite yet.
  6. Open a Pull Request to dev describing what changed and referencing the issue.
  7. A maintainer reviews, you may be asked for tweaks, and then it is merged.

docs.title: PR checklist
docs.text:
• Code follows the project conventions (see docs/docs/architecture.md).
  • No secrets, credentials, or personal data added.
  • Backend changes include a migration in infrastructure/migrations/ when the schema changes.
  • Docs are updated when behaviour is user-visible.
  • The change was checked by hand in the local stack.

docs.title: 3. Join the community
docs.text:
We coordinate on Discord — questions, ideas, bug triage and announcements happen there.

  • Join our Discord
  • Development and English/French/Spanish discussion welcome.

docs.title: Community journey and skill tree: technical plan
docs.text:
Status: proposal, not built yet. Date: 2026-10-30. Screens: the "Community journey screens" design canvas.

This plan says how to build the community journey in this codebase. The product rules (which roles exist, how they unlock, what they unlock) are in the product proposal, which will move to the docs vault as feature notes. This page covers the data, the code and the build order.

docs.title: In one paragraph
docs.text: Every member starts as Ambassador. Doing tasks unlocks community roles (Mapper, Verifier, Repairer, City lead…). A role brings permissions (approve a clinic) and app features (order spare parts). Points, earned on the community task board, unlock extra achievements and benefits but never roles. Roles pause after 6 months without activity. Lead roles are assigned by a community team admin. The whole tree is public.

docs.title: What already exists and is reused
docs.text:
Piece Where Reused for Four activity counts per member (devices registered, faults resolved, maintenance closed, people invited), in SQL routers/profile.py _metric_subqueries, _counts_for Unlock conditions (e.g. "5 faults resolved" for Repairer) Who invited whom users.invited_by (migration 025) "Invite one colleague" quest Linked Discord account users.discord_user_id (migration 027), routers/discord_link.py "Join the Discord" quest; @mentions in unlock posts Discord welcome webhook, announce_new_device config/discord.py, routers/discord_link.py "New role unlocked" posts Profile country profiles.country Local roles and team ("Mapper, Ghana") Superusers users.is_superuser, SQLAdmin Community team admins, for now Background tasks utils/background.py spawn Re-checking unlocks after an action without slowing the request Migration runner backend/migrations.py New tables, next number 028

Gaps: there is no applicant or member state today (any verified account can use the whole app), no city on profiles, no consent flags, no last-activity time.

docs.title: Naming: community roles, not roles
docs.text: The app already has org roles on org_users.role (admin, technician, clinical_staff, engineering_staff), which decide what someone can do inside one organization. Community roles are a separate thing and must never be mixed with them. In code, tables and API they are always community_role, member_role, /api/community/.... The existing /tasks page (fault and maintenance assignments) also stays as is; the new board is "community tasks".

docs.title: Data model
docs.text: One new migration, infrastructure/migrations/028_community_roles.sql, plus matching classes in models/models.py. All tables in schema fixmymedtech.

docs.title: The catalogue: community_roles
docs.text:
The tree is data, so the community team can grow it without a release.

Column Type Notes key text, primary key ambassador, mapper, repairer, city_lead… path text start, devices, people, trust, knowledge, teams, parts, leads tier int 0 to 3 scope text local (held for a country, later a city) or global (held for a team) or none unlock text auto (the app checks), claim (open, the member picks it), confirmed (needs a person to confirm one step), assigned (admins only: leads) names jsonb {"en": "Repairer", "fr": "Réparateur", "es": "Reparador"} descriptions jsonb Same shape linkedin_titles jsonb Same shape, for the share kit sort int Order inside its path active bool Hide a role without deleting history

Names live in the table, not in i18n.py, because the catalogue is edited by the community team. Everything else on the pages (buttons, headings) follows the usual i18n.py rule in en/es/fr.

docs.title: community_role_requirements
docs.text:
One row per condition. All rows of a role must be met.

Column Type Notes id uuid role_key text → community_roles kind text role (hold another role), metric (a count reaches a threshold), quest (a one-off step), confirmation (a person confirms) ref text Role key, metric key (devices_registered, faults_resolved, maintenance_performed, invites, later verifications, manuals_added…) or quest key threshold int, null For metrics

docs.title: community_role_permissions
docs.text:
Column Type Notes role_key text → community_roles permission text A key from the list in code (below)

The list of permission keys lives in code (backend/utils/community.py, PERMISSIONS), because each key is checked by a router. The table only says which role grants which key. Unknown keys are refused when saved.

docs.title: member_roles
docs.text:
Column Type Notes id uuid profile_id uuid → profiles role_key text → community_roles country, city text, null For local roles team text, null For global roles: software, data, hardware, manufacturing, partnerships, communications status text active, removed (paused is computed, see Pausing) source text auto, claim, confirmed, assigned granted_by uuid → profiles, null For confirmed and assigned roles granted_at timestamptz removed_at, removed_reason The member sees the reason

Unique on (profile_id, role_key, coalesce(country,''), coalesce(team,'')), so granting twice does nothing.

docs.title: member_quests
docs.text:
For the steps the app can't count from existing tables (watched an approval meeting, introduced yourself on Discord).

Column Type Notes profile_id uuid → profiles quest_key text intro_video, meeting_held, watched_approval_meeting… count int For quests done several times (watched 2 meetings) confirmed_by uuid → profiles, null updated_at timestamptz

Quests that can be read from existing data (profile_complete, discord_joined = users.discord_user_id is not null, consent_answered = profiles.social_consent is not null) are computed, not stored.

docs.title: community_role_changes
docs.text: An append-only log: id, actor_id, action (role_created, role_edited, role_assigned, role_removed, applicant_decided…), target (role key, member or applicant id), before and after (jsonb), reason, created_at.

docs.title: New columns on profiles
docs.text:
Column Type Why city text Local roles, members page country_trained text Member story ("I was trained in…") why_bme text, ≤ 500 Member story ("I chose biomedical engineering because…") member_status text default applicant applicant until the Ambassador quests are done, then member; staff for invited clinic staff who watched the video; refused if the meeting ends in a refusal member_since timestamptz When the quests were completed (or the migration date for existing accounts) social_consent bool, null Null = not answered yet. Asked on its own page social_consent_at timestamptz members_page_hidden bool default false The member hid their card last_active_at timestamptz For pausing

Backfill in the same migration: every existing profile gets member_status = 'member', member_since and the Ambassador role, so nobody already on the platform loses access.

docs.title: Unlock engine: backend/utils/community.py
docs.text:
One module, no framework.

  • progress(db, profile_id) -> dict: for every role, which requirements are met and how far (3 of 5). Reuses _counts_for from routers/profile.py, moved into this module or imported, so the journey page, the Network directory and the unlock rules always count the same way.
  • check_unlocks(db, profile_id) -> list[str]: grants every auto role whose requirements are all met and returns the new keys. Idempotent thanks to the unique constraint.
  • has_permission(db, profile, permission, country=None) -> bool: true if the member holds an active, not paused role that grants it (in that country, for local roles). Superusers always pass.
  • require_permission(permission): a FastAPI dependency for routers.

When it runs: after the actions that can change progress, through spawn(...) so the request is not slowed. That is device created (routers/devices.py), fault resolved and maintenance closed, invite accepted, Discord linked, profile saved. Also on every visit to the journey page, as a safety net.

On a new unlock: post to Discord with the existing welcome webhook (one line, same style as announce_new_device), and store the role key so the next page view shows the unlock screen once.

docs.title: Pausing after 6 months
docs.text: No scheduler is needed. last_active_at is updated (at most once a day) by get_current_profile in utils/profile.py. A role counts as paused when last_active_at is more than 6 months ago, computed when it is read, so the first action back un-pauses everything at once. The 5-month reminder email needs a daily job; it waits for phase 4.

docs.title: Joining: /join creates the account
docs.text: /join is the one way into the community. It creates an account straight away, but the account is a community applicant: it can only use the journey pages until the Ambassador quests are done. Then platform access opens.

docs.title: The form: /join (public, replaces /signup)
docs.text: Name, email, password, country, city, "I am a…" (biomedical engineer, student, clinician, other), organisation or school, country trained in, why you want to join, how you heard of us. A referral code in the link (/join?ref=CODE) sets invited_by, so the member who shared gets the credit. The existing email verification still applies. /signup redirects to /join.

docs.title: What the applicant sees: /community/start
docs.text:
Every page of the platform redirects an applicant here. It shows:

  1. the intro video (embedded; the quest is done when the video ends, or with an "I've watched it" button as a fallback),
  2. book a welcome meeting with a member of the community (a booking link, see below),
  3. the Ambassador quests as a checklist with progress,
  4. the Discord invite and a preview of the skill tree.

docs.title: The Ambassador quests
docs.text:
Quest Done when Checked Complete your profile Photo, country, city, country trained in, why you joined Automatic Watch the intro video The video reached its end Automatic Meet a member of the community The host marks the meeting as held Confirmed by an Approval host or the community team Join the Discord users.discord_user_id is set Automatic Answer the social media consent profiles.social_consent is not null (yes or no) Automatic

When the last one is done, the member gets Ambassador, member_status becomes member, and the platform opens with a welcome screen. "Invite a colleague" and "first device or first community task" move to the tier 1 roles, since they need the platform.

docs.title: Booking the meeting
docs.text: Phase 1 keeps it simple: one booking link (for example a shared Cal.com or Calendly page of the Approval hosts, set in COMMUNITY_BOOKING_URL), and the host records the meeting in the dashboard. A built-in calendar can come later.

docs.title: Table: community_applications
docs.text:
The join form answers and the meeting, one row per applicant, linked to their profile.

Column Type Notes profile_id uuid → profiles, primary key kind text engineer, student, clinician, other organisation, motivation, heard_from text host_id uuid → profiles, null The member who meets them meeting_at timestamptz, null meeting_held_at, meeting_confirmed_by Completes the meeting quest notes text Internal, never shown to the applicant status text open, meeting_booked, met, refused, withdrawn decision_reason text When refused created_at, updated_at timestamptz

A refused applicant keeps an account that can only see a message with the reason. Refused and withdrawn applications are deleted after 12 months.

docs.title: Gating the platform
docs.text:
• Backend: a new dependency get_member_profile in utils/profile.py: the same as get_current_profile, plus a 403 {"detail": "community_access_pending"} when member_status is not member or staff. Staff pass it, but hold no community role, so every community permission check still refuses them. Every platform router switches to it (devices, faults, maintenance, organizations, dashboard, tasks…). The profile, Discord, community and auth routes keep get_current_profile, so applicants can do their quests. Public /public/... routes don't change.
  • Frontend: require_auth in features/auth/helper.py reads member_status from the session (cached by UserContextMiddleware from /api/auth/me) and redirects applicants to /community/start. When the API answers community_access_pending, the session is refreshed and the same redirect happens.

docs.title: Existing and invited accounts
docs.text:
• Every existing account is backfilled as a member with Ambassador, so nobody loses access.
  • Clinic staff invited by a clinic (organisation invitation, routers/organizations.py) only have to watch the video before they get in (Jason, 2026-10-30). Their status becomes staff: they use the app inside their clinic with their org role (report faults, see devices, log maintenance), but hold no community role.
  • If they want more (community tasks, roles, the features roles unlock), they do the remaining Ambassador quests from the same start page: profile, meeting, Discord, consent. Then they become Ambassador and member, like everyone else.
  • The video quest is the same intro_video quest. The main video URL is COMMUNITY_INTRO_VIDEO_URL; a shorter clinic-staff video can be set separately (STAFF_INTRO_VIDEO_URL, falling back to the main one).

docs.text:
Phase 1 only adds the applicant gate above. Role permissions start in later phases, with require_permission(...):

Permission Granted by Checked in claim_verification_tasks Verifier Community task board (not built yet) decide_applicants, approve_clinics Approval host, community team Applicants tab, clinic approval receive_area_repair_requests Repairer Public "request maintenance" flow diagnose_outside_my_orgs Repairer routers/fault_reports.py steps 3 and 5, today limited to the assignee order_spare_parts Repairer only Spare parts catalogue (not built yet) publish_part_designs Part designer Parts library (not built yet) approve_part_designs Design reviewer Parts library supply_restricted_parts Certified maker (with a valid quality certificate) Spare parts catalogue manage_roles, assign_roles, view_members, view_applicants, view_role_history See the dashboard section Community admin dashboard

The fault workflow keeps its own org-based rules. A community permission can only add a way in, never remove one an org role already gives.

docs.title: The community admin dashboard: /community/admin
docs.text:
One dashboard with four tabs. What each person sees depends on their permissions, so the same pages serve the community team and the leads.

Tab What it does Permission Applicants New accounts still doing their quests: quest progress, filter by status and country, assign a host, record the meeting (which completes that quest), or refuse with a reason view_applicants, decide_applicants Members Every member with their roles, country, city, last activity and activity counts. Open a member: their roles and history, add or remove a role view_members, assign_roles Roles The tree as a list. Create a role, edit its names, path, tier, unlock type, requirements and permissions, or retire it manage_roles History Every change to roles, permissions and applications: who, what, when view_role_history

docs.title: Creating a role
docs.text:
Roles › New role opens one form:

  • names, description and LinkedIn title in English, French and Spanish,
  • path, tier, scope (local, global team, none),
  • how it unlocks: automatic, claimed by the member, confirmed by a person, or assigned by an admin,
  • requirements: rows of "hold role X", "count Y reaches N", "quest Z done", "confirmed by a holder of role W",
  • permissions: every key from PERMISSIONS as a checkbox with its plain description, grouped (community, devices and repairs, spare parts, admin).

Saving checks that every requirement points to a real role, metric or quest and that the tree has no loops. A new role starts as a draft, visible only in the dashboard, until an admin publishes it to the tree.

docs.title: Assigning a role
docs.text: From Members, open a member and click Add role: pick the role, the country or team it applies to, and a reason. The member gets a notification and the unlock screen on their next visit, and the change goes in History. Removing works the same way, and the reason is shown to the member.

docs.title: Permissions for the dashboard itself
docs.text:
Permission Given to manage_roles (edit the tree and its permissions) Community team admins only assign_roles (give or remove any role) Community team admins only view_applicants, decide_applicants Community team, Approval hosts (in their country) view_members Community team (everyone), City and Country leads (their country), Team leads (their team) view_role_history Community team

Superusers have every permission, so the first admins need nothing set up.

docs.title: Members list for leads
docs.text:
Leads open Members in the same dashboard, limited to their scope: a Country lead sees the members of their country, a Team lead the members of their team, the community team everyone.

For each member: name, photo, city, roles (with paused ones marked), member since, last active, and their actions: devices registered, faults resolved, maintenance done, people invited, community tasks done, and the date of their last action. A member's page shows the timeline of their roles and contributions.

Leads can see but not change roles. They can flag a member to the community team ("ready for Repairer", "inactive, contact them"). Email and phone are shown to leads only for members in their scope.

docs.title: Adding new roles later
docs.text:
Two cases, depending on whether the new role needs a new kind of access.

  1. A new role made of existing permissions (for example a "Trainer" who can confirm quests and create local tasks): no code, no release. A community team admin adds the role, its requirements and its permissions in the admin. It appears in the tree at once.
  2. A role that needs a new kind of access (for example "can publish training videos"): a small code change. A developer adds the permission key to PERMISSIONS in utils/community.py and one require_permission("publish_training") line on the router that does the action, in one pull request. Once it is deployed, admins attach the key to any role in the admin, as in case 1.

So the code only ever answers "what can be done", and the admin decides "who can do it". Every key has a short description in PERMISSIONS, which the admin shows next to the checkbox, so admins see what they are granting. Every change to roles and their permissions is logged (who, when, what) in a community_role_changes table, shown in the dashboard's History tab, and recorded in the decisions log.

docs.text:
Same pattern as the other features.

  • Register every router in frontend/main.py with xxx.rt.to_app(app).
  • Add ("/community", "community", _("nav.community")) to sidebar() in components.py, with a Lucide icon.
  • New strings in i18n.py for en, es and fr.
  • Add the member's role keys and permissions to what UserContextMiddleware caches from /api/auth/me, and refresh them after an unlock or an approval.
  • The tree is server-rendered HTML and CSS (a grid of cards, like the design canvas), no JS library. The screens to follow are in the "Community journey screens" design canvas.

docs.title: One app: joining the platform and the community
docs.text: The community is not a second app. It is a second half of the same app: one login, one sidebar, one profile, one task list. The screens are in the "One app: work and community together" row of the design canvas.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
sidebar() in components.py becomes grouped:

Group Links Notes (top) Home Work Devices, Faults, Tasks, Clinics Clinics is today's Groups page (/groups), renamed in the UI only; URLs stay Community My journey, Skill tree, Members Members replaces Network (/network redirects to /community/members) Admin Community admin Only when the member has a dashboard permission (bottom) Profile, language, theme
  • Links are data: each entry may carry a required permission, and sidebar() skips the ones the member lacks. Applicants see only "Start" and Profile.
  • On phones, a bottom bar with Devices, Faults, Community and Profile (Community opens My journey; the rest of the sidebar stays in the menu). It is new CSS in components.py, shown under 760 px.
  • The member's roles and permissions are cached in the session by UserContextMiddleware (as the avatar data is today), so building the sidebar costs no API call.

docs.title: Home: the bridge
docs.text:
/home (today a landing card) becomes the member's home:

  1. Next unlock card: the closest role and its progress, with what it unlocks. From GET /api/community/me.
  2. Open faults and Maintenance due: from the existing /api/dashboard/stats and fault list, five lines each.
  3. Community tasks near you: from the community task board when it exists; hidden until then.
  4. Near you this week: a short line of local activity (from the activity feed plan).

The landing card stays for visitors who are not signed in.

docs.title: One profile
docs.text: /profile and the public profile (/profile/{id}) show three things on one page: clinic memberships with their org roles (today's content), community roles with their country or team, and achievements and points. A line explains the difference: clinic roles are set by each clinic, community roles come from the skill tree. "Share my roles on LinkedIn" opens the share kit.

docs.title: One task inbox
docs.text: /tasks keeps its URL and gets two tabs: My jobs (today's fault and maintenance assignments, unchanged) and Community (the community tasks the member picked up or that their roles offer). The sidebar badge counts both. The community task board itself stays at /community/tasks.

docs.title: Work feeds progress
docs.text:
After an action that counts toward a role (device registered, fault resolved, maintenance closed, colleague invited), the page shows a small banner: "Fault resolved. 4 of 5 toward Repairer", linking to My journey.

  • The backend returns the progress with the action's response ("community": {"role": "repairer", "done": 4, "needed": 5}), computed by utils/community.py, so no second request is needed.
  • The frontend shows it with a new progress_toast() component in components.py, after the redirect that follows the form (kept for one request in the session, like a flash message).
  • If the action unlocked a role, the full unlock screen shows instead.

docs.title: Locked features stay visible
docs.text:
A feature that a role unlocks is shown to everyone, locked for those who don't have it: a dashed button with a padlock and "Unlock as Repairer", linking to the role page. Members meet the skill tree where they work.

  • One helper, locked_action(label, role_key, lang) in components.py, used wherever a gated action would appear (order spare parts, plan maintenance for a clinic, approve a clinic…).
  • The backend still refuses the action (require_permission); the locked button is only a signpost.
  • Lead and admin screens are hidden, not shown locked: only features that are part of the skill tree show a padlock.

docs.title: Look and feel
docs.text:
• One design system for both halves (the FixMyMedTech design system: tokens, badges, buttons). No separate community theme.
  • Community moments (unlock screen, progress banner, welcome) use brand-deep (#01437a) with white text, so they stand out without feeling like another product.
  • The community side follows the same i18n rule (en, es, fr) and the same "hospital words" voice.

docs.title: Build order
docs.text:
Each phase is one pull request against dev.

Phase 1: joining, Ambassador and the dashboard. Migration 028 with the catalogue seeded from the proposal, community_applications, community_role_changes and the backfill; utils/community.py (progress, has_permission, Ambassador quests and grant); /join and /community/start with the intro video and booking link; the platform gate (get_member_profile, require_auth redirect); the dashboard tabs Applicants, Members and History, and Roles read-only with assign and remove; GET /tree, GET /me, consent and story endpoints; pages journey, tree, role (read only), welcome. Existing accounts keep full access through the backfill.

Phase 1b: the role editor. Create and edit roles, requirements and permissions in the dashboard (until then, the catalogue is edited through SQLAdmin).

Phase 2: unlocking and one app. check_unlocks wired into the actions above, claiming tier 1 roles, tier 2 automatic unlocks, the unlock screen, Discord posts, share kit link. The grouped sidebar and phone bottom bar, the new home, the combined profile, the two-tab task inbox, progress banners and locked actions.

Phase 3: roles that do something. Confirmations (watched meetings), first permission checks (approvals, fault steps outside my orgs, area repair requests), link to the community task board when it exists.

Phase 4: leads and upkeep. City and country dashboards with local stats, flags from leads, pause reminders (daily job), public members page and stats for fixmymedtech.org.

Spare parts permissions wait for the parts library and catalogue features themselves.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: The repo has no test suite. Phase 1 adds backend/tests/test_community.py with pytest for the unlock engine (requirements met or not, idempotent grant, paused computation), since that logic decides who can do what. Pages are checked by hand on the local stack (docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up --build) with the seeded test users from scripts/seed_test_data.py.

docs.title: Open technical questions
docs.text:
• Community team admins are superusers for now. When the community team grows, should it become its own community role with manage_roles and assign_roles instead of superuser access?
  • Intro and staff videos are hosted on YouTube (Jason, 2026-10-30): embed with the IFrame Player API (youtube-nocookie.com) and mark the quest done on the ENDED state, keeping the "I've watched it" fallback button.
  • Gating the platform touches every router's dependency. It is a mechanical change but a wide one: phase 1 should land it in its own commit, checked page by page with an applicant account and a member account.
  • Local roles are held per country first. Are cities needed from phase 1, or can they wait until there are City leads?

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text:
All application tables live in a single PostgreSQL schema, fixmymedtech, and are created/updated by the ordered SQL files in infrastructure/migrations/, applied automatically at backend startup (tracked in fixmymedtech.schema_migrations). 000_initial_schema.sql is the base bootstrap — it creates every base table (idempotently), so even a brand-new empty database (e.g. a fresh Supabase project) migrates cleanly on first boot.

Conventions

  • Every row uses a UUID primary key (default gen_random_uuid()), so IDs never collide across environments and are safe to use in public QR URLs.
  • Users vs. profiles: authentication identity lives in users (managed by FastAPI-Users, JWTs signed with AUTH_JWT_SECRET). Per-user profile data lives in profiles, whose id mirrors users.id 1:1.
  • Storage: photo/avatar/document binaries are stored in MinIO. The tables only keep the object key (e.g. profiles/<uuid>/avatar_<hex>.jpg).
  • Timestamps use TIMESTAMPTZ (timezone-aware).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker Desktop (or Docker Engine + Compose V2)
  • Git
  • Nothing else for the local stack. Optionally, a Supabase project (or any PostgreSQL database) if you want to develop against a remote database
  • (Optional) Python 3.12 + uv / pip if you want to run services outside Docker

docs.title: 1. Clone and configure
docs.text:
git clone <repo-url> && cd fixmymedtech-app

cp .env.example .env

Edit .env and fill in:

Variable Where to find it DATABASE_URL Postgres connection string (Supabase pooler or local). postgresql+asyncpg://… DB_SCHEMA fixmymedtech (default) FRONTEND_URL http://localhost:8888 for local dev

GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=
GITHUB_CLIENT_ID=
GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET=

# SMTP (leave MAIL_SERVER blank to log emails to console instead)
MAIL_SERVER=
MAIL_PORT=587
MAIL_USERNAME=
MAIL_PASSWORD=
MAIL_FROM=noreply@fixmymedtech.org

# JWT signing secret (change in production)
AUTH_JWT_SECRET=replace-with-a-random-string

docs.title: Option A — Local stack (PostgreSQL + MinIO, no account needed)
docs.text:
Recommended for day-to-day development. Runs the whole app against a local PostgreSQL container, no Supabase project required:

docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up --build -d

This builds and starts four containers:

Service URL What it does db localhost:5432 PostgreSQL 16 (isolated pg-data volume) minio console http://localhost:9003 S3-compatible file storage backend http://localhost:8890 FastAPI REST API (also serves the app) frontend http://localhost:5003 FastHTML server-side UI

On first boot the database is initialised from infrastructure/db/init.sql, then the backend auto-applies every migration in infrastructure/migrations/ in order.

The local stack uses its own compose project (fixmymedtech-local), so its pg-data / minio-data volumes and host ports are independent of Option B below — switch between them freely without losing data.

docs.title: Option B — Supabase / remote PostgreSQL
docs.text:
If you prefer to develop against your Supabase project, set DATABASE_URL in .env (see section 1) and run:

docker compose up --build -d

This builds and starts three containers:

Service URL What it does backend http://localhost:8888 FastAPI REST API frontend http://localhost:5001 FastHTML server-side UI minio console http://localhost:9001 S3-compatible file storage

Once running:

  • App: http://localhost:8890 with Option A, http://localhost:8888 with Option B
  • API docs (Swagger): /docs on the same address
  • Admin portal: /admin/ on the same address (superuser only — see below)

The local stack (Option A) uses 8890 / 5003 so it can run at the same time as Option B on 8888 / 5001. Change them with LOCAL_BACKEND_PORT / LOCAL_FRONTEND_PORT in .env. - MinIO console: http://localhost:9003 with Option A, http://localhost:9001 with Option B (creds minioadmin/minioadmin unless overridden)

docs.title: First-time setup — create a superuser
docs.text:
After the containers are up, create your first admin account:

docker compose exec backend python utils/create_superuser.py

(With the local stack, add -f docker-compose.local.yml: docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml exec backend python utils/create_superuser.py)

The script asks for email, name, and password interactively. It creates the user (with profile + default org) and marks them as superuser.

To promote an existing user to superuser, run the script with their email — it will update their password and grant superuser access.

Automated (recommended for servers/deploys): instead set SUPERUSER_EMAIL, SUPERUSER_PASSWORD (and optional SUPERUSER_NAME) in your environment — the backend then creates/promotes that admin automatically on every startup, right after applying migrations. The dev/prod deploy workflows already pass these through from the DEV_SUPERUSER_* / PROD_SUPERUSER_* GitHub secrets.

docs.title: Send invitations & verification emails
docs.text:
Once logged in as a superuser at /admin/:

Feature Where What it does Invite a user /admin-panel/invite Creates an account and sends a verification email with a link to set their password Resend verification User detail page → "Send Verification Email" button Re-sends the verification email to an unverified user Password reset User detail page → "Send Password Reset" button Sends a password reset link to the user

Note: When MAIL_SERVER is not configured (default for local dev), emails are logged to the backend console instead of being sent. Check docker compose logs backend to see the email content and verification links.

docs.title: 3. Project structure
docs.text: See Architecture for the full layout, request flow, and the frontend feature pattern.

docs.title: 4. Admin portal
docs.text:
The admin portal at /admin/ uses SQLAdmin to provide a browsable database UI.

Who can access: Only users with is_superuser = true in the fixmymedtech.users table.

Available models:

Model What it shows Users Auth accounts (email, is_active, is_verified, is_superuser) Profiles User profiles (username, full_name) Org Users User↔Organization links and roles Organizations Hospitals, clinics, etc. Device Categories Equipment categories (seeded from CSV) Devices All registered equipment Documents Manuals, guides, videos linked to devices Fault Reports Submitted fault reports Maintenance Logs Maintenance history

docs.title: 5. Database migrations
docs.text:
Migrations live in infrastructure/migrations/ and are named NNN_description.sql. They run automatically on backend startup in numeric order. Each migration is recorded in fixmymedtech.schema_migrations so it only runs once.

To add a new migration:

# Pick the next number after the highest existing file
cat > infrastructure/migrations/026_my_change.sql << 'SQL'
ALTER TABLE fixmymedtech.devices ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS warranty_end DATE;
SQL

Rebuild and restart the backend container (up --build -d backend) and it will apply automatically. Never edit a migration that has already been applied; add a new one. Update backend/models/models.py to match.

docs.title: Create a new API endpoint
docs.text:
1. Add your route in the relevant backend/routers/*.py file
  2. Use Depends(current_active_user) for auth, or Depends(get_current_profile) for profile + org context
  3. Register the router in backend/main.py if it's a new file

docs.title: Add a new database model
docs.text:
1. Define the model in backend/models/models.py
  2. Create a migration SQL in infrastructure/migrations/
  3. Add a ModelView in backend/main.py for the admin portal

docs.title: Run a one-off DB query
docs.text:
docker compose exec backend python -c "
import asyncio
from config.db_config import engine
from sqlalchemy import text

async def main():
    async with engine.begin() as conn:
        result = await conn.execute(text('SELECT count(*) FROM fixmymedtech.users'))
        print('Users:', result.scalar())

asyncio.run(main())
"

docs.title: Register a device
docs.text:
How to register a medical device in FixMyMedTech from a phone, from scanning its QR label to the device page. The video is narrated and available in English, Spanish and French.

EnglishEspañolFrançais

  1. Sign in with your email and password.
  2. Scan the QR label: tap Scan QR code and point the camera at the device's QR label.
  3. No camera? Type the code printed under the QR label and tap Submit.
  4. Step 1 of 6: Basic information. Choose the category (required) and add the manufacturer, model, serial number, device name and manufacture year.
  5. Step 2: Photo (optional). Take a photo or choose one from your phone.
  6. Step 3: Location. Tap Capture current location, pick the healthsite (or search and add one), and say where the device sits in the clinic. Check the responsible organization.
  7. Step 4: Acquisition & maintenance (optional). How the device was acquired, its status, and its last and next maintenance dates.
  8. Step 5: Notes. Anything the next technician should know.
  9. Step 6: Manuals (optional). Search iFixit and tick manuals to attach, then tap Register device.

The device now has its own page, linked to its QR label. From there you can report faults and log maintenance.

  1. Inicia sesión con tu correo electrónico y tu contraseña.
  2. Escanea la etiqueta QR: pulsa Escanear QR y apunta la cámara a la etiqueta QR del equipo.
  3. ¿Sin cámara? Escribe el código impreso bajo la etiqueta QR y pulsa Enviar.
  4. Paso 1 de 6: Información básica. Elige la categoría (obligatoria) y añade fabricante, modelo, número de serie, nombre y año de fabricación.
  5. Paso 2: Foto (opcional). Haz una foto o elige una de tu móvil.
  6. Paso 3: Ubicación. Pulsa Capturar ubicación actual, elige el centro de salud (o búscalo y añádelo) e indica dónde está el equipo. Comprueba la organización responsable.
  7. Paso 4: Adquisición y mantenimiento (opcional). Cómo se adquirió el equipo, su estado y las fechas del último y el próximo mantenimiento.
  8. Paso 5: Notas. Lo que el próximo técnico deba saber.
  9. Paso 6: Manuales (opcional). Busca en iFixit y marca los manuales que quieras adjuntar; después pulsa Registrar dispositivo.

El equipo ya tiene su propia página, vinculada a su etiqueta QR. Desde ahí puedes reportar fallas y registrar mantenimientos.

  1. Connectez-vous avec votre e-mail et votre mot de passe.
  2. Scannez l'étiquette QR : touchez Scanner le QR code et visez l'étiquette QR de l'appareil.
  3. Pas de caméra ? Saisissez le code imprimé sous l'étiquette QR et touchez Envoyer.
  4. Étape 1 sur 6 : Informations de base. Choisissez la catégorie (obligatoire), puis le fabricant, le modèle, le numéro de série, le nom et l'année de fabrication.
  5. Étape 2 : Photo (facultatif). Prenez une photo ou choisissez-en une sur votre téléphone.
  6. Étape 3 : Emplacement. Touchez Capturer l'emplacement actuel, choisissez l'établissement de santé (ou recherchez-le et ajoutez-le) et indiquez où se trouve l'appareil. Vérifiez l'organisation responsable.
  7. Étape 4 : Acquisition & maintenance (facultatif). Mode d'acquisition, statut, dates de la dernière et de la prochaine maintenance.
  8. Étape 5 : Notes. Ce que le prochain technicien doit savoir.
  9. Étape 6 : Manuels (facultatif). Cherchez sur iFixit et cochez les manuels à joindre, puis touchez Enregistrer l'appareil.

L'appareil a maintenant sa propre page, liée à son étiquette QR. Depuis cette page, vous pouvez signaler des pannes et noter la maintenance.

Device photo in the videos: Philips Respironics oxygen concentrator by i_am_jim, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0. Silent, shorter versions of each video are in docs/docs/videos/ (register-device-<lang>-mute.mp4).

docs.title: Report a fault and get it repaired
docs.text:
How a fault goes from the first report to the repair. Each step is done by a different person, and every step is recorded on the fault's timeline. The video is narrated and available in English, Spanish and French.

EnglishEspañolFrançais

  1. Report (anyone). Scan the device's QR label and tap Report fault. Describe the problem, add a photo if you can, choose the severity and tap Submit fault report. High or Critical marks the device as out of service.
  2. Assign (maintenance admin). The admin of the organization that maintains the device finds the fault under Faults, picks a technician and taps Assign.
  3. Diagnose and quote (technician). The technician writes the diagnosis and an estimated price, then taps Send for approval.
  4. Approve (healthsite admin). The admin of the hospital where the device is reviews the diagnosis and price, and taps Approve (or Reject with a comment, which sends it back to the technician).
  5. Repair (technician). On site, the technician taps I have started the repair. Once it's fixed, they write what was done and the final price, and tap Close the fault.

The device goes back to Operational once no other serious fault is open on it.

  1. Reportar (cualquier persona). Escanea la etiqueta QR del equipo y pulsa Reportar falla. Describe el problema, añade una foto si puedes, elige la gravedad y pulsa Enviar reporte de falla. Alta o Crítica marca el equipo como fuera de servicio.
  2. Asignar (admin. de mantenimiento). El administrador de la organización que mantiene el equipo encuentra la falla en Fallas, elige un técnico y pulsa Asignar.
  3. Diagnóstico y cotización (técnico/a). El técnico escribe el diagnóstico y un precio estimado, y pulsa Enviar a aprobación.
  4. Aprobar (admin. del centro de salud). El administrador del hospital donde está el equipo revisa el diagnóstico y el precio, y pulsa Aprobar (o Rechazar con un comentario, que lo devuelve al técnico).
  5. Reparar (técnico/a). En el lugar, el técnico pulsa Ya comencé la reparación. Cuando está arreglado, anota lo que se hizo y el precio final, y pulsa Cerrar la falla.

El equipo vuelve a Operativo cuando no le queda ninguna otra falla grave abierta.

  1. Signaler (tout le monde). Scannez l'étiquette QR de l'appareil et touchez Signaler un problème. Décrivez le problème, ajoutez une photo si possible, choisissez la gravité et touchez Envoyer le signalement. Élevée ou Critique met l'appareil hors service.
  2. Assigner (admin. maintenance). L'administrateur de l'organisation qui assure la maintenance trouve la panne dans Pannes, choisit un technicien et touche Assigner.
  3. Diagnostic et devis (technicien·ne). Le technicien rédige le diagnostic et un prix estimé, puis touche Envoyer pour approbation.
  4. Approuver (admin. de l'établissement). L'administrateur de l'hôpital où se trouve l'appareil examine le diagnostic et le prix, puis touche Approuver (ou Rejeter avec un commentaire, ce qui renvoie la panne au technicien).
  5. Réparer (technicien·ne). Sur place, le technicien touche J'ai commencé la réparation. Une fois l'appareil réparé, il note ce qui a été fait et le prix final, et touche Clôturer la panne.

L'appareil redevient Opérationnel dès qu'aucune autre panne grave n'est ouverte.

Device photo in the videos: Philips Respironics oxygen concentrator by i_am_jim, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0. Silent, shorter versions of each video are in docs/docs/videos/ (report-fault-<lang>-mute.mp4).

docs.title: FixMyMedTech — Running Without Docker
docs.text: The recommended way to develop is the Docker stack described in Getting Started. This page covers running the backend and frontend directly on your machine, which gives faster reloads while you edit Python code.

docs.title: 1. Start the infrastructure
docs.text:
The backend needs PostgreSQL and MinIO. The easiest option is to start only those two containers from the local stack:

cp .env.example .env
docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml up -d db minio

This exposes PostgreSQL on localhost:5432 (user/password postgres, database fixmymedtech) and MinIO on localhost:9002 (console on localhost:9003, minioadmin / minioadmin).

A fresh PostgreSQL volume is initialised from infrastructure/db/init.sql. You can also point DATABASE_URL at a Supabase project instead. In that case the schema is created by the migrations on the first backend start.

docs.title: 2. Backend (FastAPI)
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.12.

cd backend
pip install -r requirements.txt

export DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/fixmymedtech
export DB_SCHEMA=fixmymedtech
export MINIO_ENDPOINT=localhost:9002
export MIGRATIONS_DIR=../infrastructure/migrations

uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8888
  • API: http://localhost:8888/api/...
  • Swagger: http://localhost:8888/docs
  • Admin portal: http://localhost:8888/admin/

Pending migrations are applied on startup. MIGRATIONS_DIR must point to infrastructure/migrations relative to where you run the backend. The default is infrastructure/migrations, which matches the Docker image layout.

Create a superuser with python utils/create_superuser.py, or set SUPERUSER_EMAIL / SUPERUSER_PASSWORD before starting.

docs.title: 3. Frontend (FastHTML)
docs.text:
cd frontend
pip install -r requirements.txt

export API_URL=http://localhost:8888
export SESSION_SECRET=any-random-string

python main.py

The app runs at http://localhost:5001 with live reload.

Outside Docker, open the frontend directly on port 5001. The backend's UI proxy forwards to the hostname frontend:5001, which only resolves inside the compose network, so http://localhost:8888/ will not show the app.

docs.title: 4. Seed test data (optional)
docs.text:
python scripts/seed_test_data.py

This creates demo organizations and users (all with password Pass123!) in the database at DATABASE_URL, which defaults to postgresql+asyncpg://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/fixmymedtech.

docs.title: 5. Documentation (MkDocs)
docs.text:
cd docs
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

The docs are served at http://localhost:8000.
